1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nd2 Nc6 4.c3 dxe4 5.Nx.strategy: Takes the pawn back and centralises the knight, with the c-pawn already on c3 to support d4. The knight eyes the d6, f6 and c5 squares, and White keeps more space in the centre as the game opens.

Strikes at d4 for a third time and opens the diagonal of the queen's bishop, so White has to settle the centre at once. Black chooses an open game with quick development over passive solidity; the cost is a looser pawn structure.
1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nd2 Nc6 4.c3 dxe4 5.Nx.name: French Defence: Tarrasch Variation, Guimard Defence, Thunderbunny Variation
